To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
wortmannin inhibits uptake of ligand by reducing the number of surface mannose receptors, by inhibiting internalization of receptor-ligands and by inhibiting transport from early to late endosomes.

the inhibition of phosphatidyloinositide 3-kinase by wortmannin causes a decrease in the number of surface mannose receptors, reduced internalization of ligand, increased recycling, reduced transport of ligand from early endosomes to lysosomal degradation and reduced size of early-endosomal vesicles in rat liver endothelia cells.

wortmannin inhibits the uptake of ovalbumin by rat liver endothelial (LEC) cells via a mechanism involving both a decrease in the number of cell surface mannose receptors and a reduced rate of internalization of receptor-ligands.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of wortmanninsensitive phosphatidylinositide metabolism in the endocytosis, recycling and intralysosomal transport of ligands in rat liver endothelia cells.
the role of the PI 3-kinase pathway in the endocytosis of mannose receptor ligands.
the involvement of phosphatidyinositol 3-kinase in the endocytosis and transport of macromolecules in rat LECs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
wortmannin affects the endocytic uptake of ovalbumin by reducing the number of surface mannose receptors and inhibiting the internalization and transport of the receptor-ligand complex.
wortmannin inhibits the uptake of ovalbumin via the mannose-receptor by reducing the number of surface receptor and by decreasing the rate of internalization.

wortmannin inhibits the uptake of ovalbumin in LECs by reducing the number of surface mannose receptors, by decreasing the rate of mannose-receptor-ligand internalisation and by blocking intracellular transport of internalized ovalbumin from endosomes to late endosomes/lysosomes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

wortmannin inhibits the uptake and degradation of ligand by preventing ligand internalization, inhibiting transport of ligand from early to late endocytic compartments and inhibiting fusion of endosomal compartments with lysosomes.
wortmannin treatment inhibits endocytosis by reducing the rate of internalization and by blocking transport from early endosomes to late endosomes.
the PI-kinase inhibitor wortmannin affects the endocytic trafficking of ligand in LECs by inhibiting the formation of early endosomes and preventing ligand transport to lysosomes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the phosphoinositide kinases, PI3-kinase and PI4-kinase, play a key role in the early endocytic pathway of the liver endothelium.
phosphoinositides play an important role in regulating the different steps in the endosomal pathway.

the endocytic uptake of ovalbumin in LECs is regulated by phosphoinositide signalling, and that wortmannin inhibits both the internalization of the mannose receptor and the transport of internalized ligands to lysosomes, thereby affecting both the degradation and recycling of the ligand.
